question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the population are smokers. A smoker has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn></math> times more chances to develop lung cancer then a non-smoker. A person is diagnosed with lung cancer and the probability that this person is a smoker is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>k</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math>.Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Given,

In a city, 25% of the population is smoker

So, Psmoker=0.25

Pnon-smoking=0.75

And smoker has 27 times more chance of being diagnosed with lung cancer,

So, if PLung cancernon-smoker=p then PLung cancersmoker=27p,

Now,  a person is selected at random and found to be diagnosed with lung cancer,

So, total probability of having a lung cancer will be 

PLung cancer=0.25×27p+0.75×p

So the probability of him being smoker (using bayes' theorem) will be PsmokerLung cancer=0.25×27p0.25×27p+0.75×p=2730=910

Now comparing with k10=910,

Then the value of k will be 9.
